newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria, Romania in study for new Danube bridge.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, Romania in study for new Danube bridge.

text.p: Bulgaria and Romania signed on Tuesday a protocol to evaluate two options for the location of a new bridge over the Danube river, Bulgarian state radio said.
The two Balkan countries vowed last month to renew negotiations on the planned bridge after years of disagreements over its location.

"The two sides signed a protocol ...for two locations where a bridge could be constructed," the radio said, adding that the two countries' deputy transport ministers met in Bulgaria's Danube port of Rousse.
The proposed locations are between the port of Vidin and the Romanian town of Calafat near the Serbian border and the town of Belene and Choara, the radio said.

A feasibility study by a British firm indicated that the western position would be more suitable. Bulgaria insists on a Vidin-Calafat bridge, while Romania was in favour of a bridge in the eastern part of the river.
The new bridge is expected to ease Europe's access to the east as part of the European Union's trans-European network. It is estimated to cost more than $400 million.
The two countries are now connected by only one congested bridge and operate two ferry links across the Danube.
